title: Beware of tokens purported to be associated with licensed stablecoin issuers
summary: On 28 April 2026, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) published a press release titled 'Beware of tokens purported to be associated with licensed stablecoin issuers.' HKMA's website returned no retrievable content on every fetch attempt made while drafting and independently verifying this card, and web searches for the release's exact title found no readable copy on any other official Hong Kong government domain, so its substantive content -- including any specific tokens or entities named, and what advice it gives the public -- could not be confirmed against primary source text. Based on the title alone, the release appears to be a public warning that some tokens circulating claim an association with HKMA-licensed stablecoin issuers, without HKMA confirming that association is genuine. This card should be revisited, and its content checked directly against the primary source, once HKMA's website is reachable.
why_it_matters: Based on its title, this appears to be HKMA policing the edges of its own stablecoin-issuer licensing regime, warning the public that some circulating tokens claim an association with a licensed issuer that HKMA has not confirmed is genuine -- though the release's substantive details could not be confirmed against primary source text. For a newcomer, it is a reminder that being 'associated' with a licensed issuer is a specific, checkable regulatory fact rather than something to take on a token promoter's word.

citations.quote: Beware of tokens purported to be associated with licensed stablecoin issuers
